data.narrative:
Agility Robotics, a Series E robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $400M+, is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private and 1 public peer. Primary private comparables include Divergent ($2.3B, Series E), Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Locus Robotics ($2.0B, Series F), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The stage-progression method applies a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E advancement to the $385M total-raised proxy, implying $539M. The peer-median method anchors to the median valuation of the four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables at $2.0B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.3B. These comparables represent demonstrated market appetite for robotics platforms at scale.

The triangulated valuation range is $458M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The wide spread reflects genuine uncertainty between method outputs: stage-progression conservatively suggests $539M based on capital deployed, while peer multiples imply substantially higher valuations. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Agility's product differentiation, unit economics, and market traction align with higher-valued peers versus earlier-stage cost structures. Resolution of this gap will depend on revenue trajectories and capital efficiency relative to the comp set.
